summary: Discovery focused on Aurora's inference needs for a fraud-detection ML feature: they prefer Dedicated capacity for data isolation and predictable throughput, with occasional burst traffic. Key concerns were network isolation, KMS integration, SOC2, and scaling/rollback strategy. Agreement to run benchmarks in staging and share pricing/options.
transcript:
Header: 2026-12-30 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~54m
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Laura (Redwood SE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Evelyn (CTO), Marco (Head of ML), Priya (Security), Ben (Infra)

Summary: quick discovery on dedicated capacity for Aurora's realtime fraud inference. They run models for transaction scoring, want sub-100ms p50, but more importantly p95 under 500ms, privacy/regulatory requirements mean dedicated or private mandatory for production.

00:00 Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, happy holidays - I'm Samir from Redwood, this is Laura and Marcus from our infra team, want to run through your workload, requirements, and what dedicated would look like.
00:12 Evelyn: Thanks Samir, yeah we appreciate it. Quick context: Aurora's building a real-time fraud scoring microservice, currently running on in-house k8s with Triton + huggingface models, looking to move to a managed dedicated GPU fleet to reduce ops and get consistent latency.
00:30 Marco: Hi - our model is a transformer condensed to a 6B-ish family, typically 512 tokens, average request 250 tokens, but inference uses a batch of one mostly for latency. We get bursts during morning settlement windows up to ~1.2k qps, sustained around 200-300 qps.
00:50 Laura: Got it. Do you have quantized variants in prod already? or are you looking for us to help with that?
00:56 Marco: We're experimenting with 4-bit quant; quality regressions have been small but still evaluating.
01:04 Priya: Security is key - we need VPC-level network isolation, customer-managed KMS, audit logs, SSO (SAML), and SOC 2 compliance. Also data residency for EU accounts.
01:20 Marcus: That's standard for Dedicated and Private deployments - Dedicated gives you tenant isolation on the serving layer, and we can enable private networking and KMS. For Private on-prem we support air-gapped but that's a bigger lift.
01:34 Ben: On autoscaling - we don't want cold-start blips during spikes. How does Redwood handle burst?
01:40 Laura: We have reserved capacity pools plus burst capacity. For example you can commit to N GPUs for guaranteed throughput and then allow bursting to shared capacity. There's also pre-warm policies and pinned VMs for hot paths.
01:55 Marco: Practically, are spikes routed to a compatible model variant or do you queue? we need sub-second p95.
02:02 Marcus: We can route to a slightly smaller quantized variant automatically as fallback, or use cross-tenant burst if you opt into burst. There's also smart routing by policy - latency-first or cost-first.
02:18 Evelyn: What's the SLA on Dedicated? and what about fallbacks if dedicated pool is saturated?
02:24 Samir: Our Dedicated offering includes an SLA for uptime and throughput tiers depending on commit. If pool saturated, policy-based fallbacks can hit a compatible hosted model (read: same architecture but maybe different quantization) or queue with backpressure. We can show p99 vs p95 numbers in the benchmark.
02:45 Priya: Can you confirm KMS/HSM integration? we need customer-managed keys and that all logs are encrypted at rest.
02:52 Marcus: Yes, Dedicated and Private support bringing-your-own-KMS (AWS KMS or cloud HSM), and logs are encrypted. We also provide audit log streaming for SIEM.
03:05 Marco: How do you size reserved GPUs? is it based on peak qps or sustained throughput?
03:12 Laura: Typically we size for sustained throughput and then add headroom for latency SLOs. For example if you need 300 sustained qps with p95 < 500ms, we calculate tokens/sec and model latency on target GPU to estimate required GPUs, then add a buffer for burst.
03:28 Ben: Any recommendations for batch sizes? right now we mostly do batch=1 but could benefit from microbatching.
03:33 Marcus: Continuous batching helps cost but can increase latency - we recommend dynamic batching with a small max batch for tail latency control. For fraud scoring, microbatch of 2-4 with strict timeouts can help.
03:50 Marco: How about cost delta between Dedicated and Hosted? rough ballpark per token/ per hour?
03:55 Samir: We'll send tiered pricing. Generally dedicated has a monthly reserved fee plus a lower per-token compute rate; burst usage is priced higher. For large volumes Dedicated reduces unit cost compared to Hosted, but exact depends on commit and model family.
04:12 Evelyn: For our compliance we may require VPC-peering and no egress to public internet. Is that possible?
04:18 Marcus: Yes - you can have private endpoints, VPC peering, and restrict egress. For Private deployments you get entire control; Dedicated gives strong isolation but control plane is Redwood-managed unless you opt for Private.
04:32 Priya: Do you provide SOC2 and ISO docs? we need them for procurement.
04:36 Samir: Yes, we'll share SOC2 and ISO attestation and our security whitepaper. We'll also include the dedicated architecture diagram.
04:45 Marco: Any limitations on model size or kv-cache? our inference uses a KV cache for session histories.
04:50 Laura: We support KV cache management; dedicated can pin cache on GPUs and tune eviction. Model size limitations depend on GPU memory; we support multi-GPU sharding for large models.
05:05 Ben: How long does provisioning take for a dedicated pool?
05:09 Marcus: Depending on capacity and region, provisioning for reserved pool typically 2-5 business days; for Private on-prem it's longer. We can sometimes accelerate for enterprise deals.
05:20 Evelyn: Can we run a pilot? want to validate p95 and failure modes.
05:24 Samir: Absolutely - typical path is a 4-week pilot with a small reserved pool + benchmark scripts. We'll run benchmarks in our staging region against your sample traffic.
05:34 Marco: For the pilot we'd provide sample payloads, and want to measure p50/p95, concurrency, cost per 1M tokens.
05:40 Laura: That's perfect. We'll instrument traces and share a dashboard in Redwood Console.
05:46 Priya: On logging, can we get raw request/response logs redacted and stored in our S3?
05:52 Marcus: Yes, log export to customer S3 with redaction rules is supported for Dedicated and Private.
05:58 Ben: Any third-party network appliances supported for egress filtering?
06:03 Laura: You can front with your own LB/appliances in peered VPC; we can also integrate with partner firewalls.
06:12 Evelyn: Timeline wise procurement needs to sign by mid-Jan to be in production by March. Is that feasible?
06:18 Samir: Yes, if pilot starts early Jan and procurement/contracting goes smoothly we can target production in March.
06:26 Marco: Anything else on performance - do you have benchmarks for 6B models on A100 vs H100?
06:32 Marcus: We have perf profiles; H100 gives better throughput for long sequences and better kernel support. We'll include sample benchmarks for 6B models on A100/H100 in the pack.
06:45 Marco: Are you able to do quantization-aware kernel selection? sometimes we see worse latency on quantized kernels.
06:52 Laura: The runtime picks kernels based on model arch, seq len and quant level; we also test in the bench to pick the best variant. Occasionally we recommend FP16 for p95 sensitive workloads.
07:05 Samir: Ok recap - next steps: we'll send pricing and security docs (SOC2/ISO), Laura/Marcus will set up a benchmark in staging, and Aurora will send sample traffic + QPS target. We'll aim for pilot in early Jan.
07:20 Evelyn: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
07:24 Meeting ends.

Notes: transcript includes typical transcription noise e.g., "KV cash" or "Redwood Dedicate" in auto-generated text; speaker labels sometimes abbreviated. Action items captured above.
